newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open weak, block deals dominate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open weak, block deals dominate.

text.p: Singapore shares opened weak on Thursday continuing a bout of profit taking which reversed a pre-budget rally at the start of the week.
"The market is a bit quieter than yesterday, but there is still a bit of selling going on," said a broker with a Singapore firm.
Dealers said sentiment was also dented due to the sharp fall in Wall Street stocks overnight.
"Sentiment has turned a bit negative, so most investors are just sitting on the sidelines," said the broker.
After an hour of trading, the Straits Times Industrial index was down 6.75 points to 1,976.22. Total market volume was 28.84 million units with 146 losers beating 28 gainers.
Index linked Keppel Corp was among the actives with a 2.2 million block married at between Singapore $6.67 to S$6.78. The shares were being quoted at S$6.60, down 15 cents.
Analysts say there was interest in Keppel as it was likely to start redeveloping its former shipyard site next year.

Singapore Telecom saw a married block of 701,000 units done at between S$2.70-S$2.71. DBS Land also saw a block of 1.07 million units changing hands at between S$4.61-S$4.75. It was down six cents to S$4.54.
Bread maker QAF Ltd was suspending pending the release of a company announcement. Five lots managed to change hands at S$1.80, up four cents, before the shares were suspended.
Leading early losers was City Developments which shed 60 cents to S$13.10
